- If sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to underpredict sharp upward moves; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% for the next 5–7 days.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and model shows gradual decline, model often underreacts to sudden drops; add 2–5% downward bias in early days of bearish sentiment.
- After a spike in price (e.g., >75), model frequently overcorrects and forecasts a prolonged decline; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for 3–5 days post-spike.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish (or vice versa), model lags by 2–4 days; adjust forecast to align with sentiment change 1–2 days ahead.
- Model consistently underestimates mean reversion in 30-day horizon; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias in final 5–7 days if sentiment is neutral or mildly bullish.
- If sentiment is high and price is trending upward, model often fails to capture momentum; increase forecast slope by 1–2% for 3–5 days ahead.
- If sentiment is low and price is trending downward, model often overestimates recovery; reduce forecast by 1–3% for 3–5 days ahead.
